  PROBLEM: The base-fetch procedure does not require the fetch to succeed before comparing against `origin/<base>`, so a failed fetch can leave a stale ref and cause the diff to miss guard changes.
  WHY: The session can continue under the outdated guard; callers that do not pre-fetch the base and tests that only exercise successful fetches leave this failure mode exposed.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 181 (new step 1) — the procedure text after `git fetch origin <base>` | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Step 1 has no failure handler for `git fetch origin <base>`, so the next diff can treat a stale remote-tracking ref as “no drift.”
  WHY: The session can move to step 2 without inspecting the fetch result and enter “nothing to do,” despite the check being intended to prevent this failure mode.
